Not a governed metric: no metric splits average order value by first-time vs returning customer, so I computed it from gold.customer_lifetime as total order value ÷ total orders per group (the average_order_value_eur definition: revenue over non-cancelled orders), classifying customers whose first order fell in 1–10 October 2026 as first-time buyers and customers with two or more lifetime orders as returning customers. A first-time buyer's order averaged €41.00 (7 orders, €287.00) versus €92.89 for a returning customer (210 orders, €19,506.59), so €51.89 less on average, over 1–10 October 2026 (returning-customer values use lifetime aggregates, as no per-order table is available).
ROAS was about 20.56 (booking-value EUR per ad-spend EUR) for September 2026, from 1 September to 30 September 2026 (booking value 128,900.00 EUR against ad spend 6,270.00 EUR).

Every €100 of social ad spend got about 1.9 leads (40 leads on €2,100 of social ad spend) in September 2026 (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Yes — slightly. Average daily revenue was about €389.71 on Saturdays and Sundays versus €385.88 on the other days (each weekday occurs six times in the six-week period Mon 17 Aug – Sun 27 Sep 2026, so weekend = 12 days, weekdays = 30 days, from revenue_eur totals grouped by day of week).

  SELECT generate_series('2026-09-01'::date, '2026-09-30'::date, interval '1 day')::date AS d
),
calls AS (
  SELECT call_date, sum(calls_labelled) AS calls
  FROM gold.call_signals_daily
  WHERE call_date BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'
  GROUP BY call_date
)
SELECT round(avg(coalesce(c.calls, 0))::numeric, 2) AS avg_calls_per_day
FROM days d
LEFT JOIN calls c ON c.call_date = d.d;

countries AS (

    CROSS JOIN countries c
),
sales AS (
    SELECT order_date, country, revenue_eur
    FROM exposed.sales_by_country_daily
    WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2026-08-17' AND '2026-10-02'
),
joined AS (
    SELECT cal.order_date, cal.country, COALESCE(s.revenue_eur, 0) AS revenue_eur
    FROM calendar cal

)
SELECT country,

GROUP BY country
ORDER BY avg_daily_revenue_eur ASC

WITH weeks AS (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN activity_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-07' AND DATE '2026-09-13' THEN 'prior'
         WHEN activity_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-14' AND DATE '2026-09-20' THEN 'current' END AS wk,
    ad_spend_eur
  FROM gold.marketing_daily
  WHERE activity_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-07' AND DATE '2026-09-20'
)
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN wk = 'current' THEN ad_spend_eur ELSE 0 END) AS current_week_spend_eur,
  SUM(CASE WHEN wk = 'prior' THEN ad_spend_eur ELSE 0 END) AS prior_week_spend_eur,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN wk = 'prior' THEN ad_spend_eur ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE round((
         SUM(CASE WHEN wk = 'current' THEN ad_spend_eur ELSE 0 END)
         - SUM(CASE WHEN wk = 'prior' THEN ad_spend_eur ELSE 0 END)
       )::numeric / SUM(CASE WHEN wk = 'prior' THEN ad_spend_eur ELSE 0 END) * 100, 2)
  END AS wow_growth_percent
FROM weeks;

WITH orders_range AS (
  SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount,
         CASE WHEN MIN(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) IS NULL THEN 'first' ELSE 'returning' END AS buyer_type
  FROM silver.orders
  WHERE order_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-10-01' AND DATE '2026-10-10'
)
SELECT 
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN buyer_type='first' THEN amount END)::numeric,2) AS avg_first,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN buyer_type='returning' THEN amount END)::numeric,2) AS avg_returning,
  ROUND((AVG(CASE WHEN buyer_type='returning' THEN amount END) - AVG(CASE WHEN buyer_type='first' THEN amount END))::numeric,2) AS diff_euros,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE buyer_type='first') AS first_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE buyer_type='returning') AS returning_count
FROM orders_range;

WITH ordered_orders AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        order_ts,
        LAG(order_ts) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_ts) AS prev_ts
    FROM silver.orders
    WHERE order_ts >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND order_ts < DATE '2026-10-01'

)
SELECT
    percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY gap_hours) AS median_gap_hours
FROM gaps;
